newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco talks in Manitoba delayed slightly.
newsitem.headline: Inco talks in Manitoba delayed slightly.

text.p: Inco Ltd and the union representing locked out workers at its Manitoba facility have delayed renewed negotiations until Thursday afternoon.
Talks were to resume Thursday morning, but negotiators needed some extra prepartion time, said Bob Desjarlais, president of local 6166 of the United Steelworkers of America.
"We don't want to rush into anything," said Desjarlais. "My feeling is we're only going to get one crack at it."
Inco locked out almost 1,400 workers on September 15 after the union members rejected the company's latest contract offer.
There have been no direct talks since then. The main issues are wages and shift scheduling.
If the parties are not able to reach an agreement in this session, "then I think we're in for a long haul," said Desjarlais.
The Thompson, Manitoba facility produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year, about 20 percent of Inco's total output.
"We're just going to let things unfold," said Inco spokesman Mark Tessier.
